target.title: [codex] Allow reply_payload_sending to add portable buttons
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins need a portable way to add presentation buttons to outbound replies before channel rendering, without expanding the broad `message_sending` hook into a transport/presentation mutation API.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps `message_sending` focused on the logical outbound message contract and uses the existing `reply_payload_sending` boundary for presentation-level mutation. Buttons live on `ReplyPayload.presentation`, and `reply_payload_sending` runs after reply payload normalization but before channel rendering, which makes it the right place for portable button decoration.

OCA compared the earlier `message_sending` direction against this implementation and agreed the current `reply_payload_sending` approach is cleaner: it avoids adding payload shape, outbound metadata, precedence rules, and cross-channel rendering promises to the public `message_sending` API.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can add portable presentation buttons through `reply_payload_sending`. Existing `message_sending` plugins keep their current text/cancel/routing behavior. Channel renderers still own native button/select rendering, fallback text, and transport limits.

## Evidence

Current head: `b419d6a64366ef5c23f1795f165fe17c5af0861b`.

Latest repair validation on current head `b419d6a64366ef5c23f1795f165fe17c5af0861b`:

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts --reporter=verbose` - 90 tests passed
- `pnpm lint:extensions:no-relative-outside-package`
- `pnpm lint:extensions:no-src-outside-plugin-sdk`
- `pnpm test:extensions:package-boundary` - 116 plugins compiled, 2 canaries passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine codex --model gpt-5.5 --thinking high` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings

Validation on the final branch:

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `rg` guard for removed `message_sending` payload/outbound metadata API
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - 100 tests passed

Live Telegram proof:

- Scenario: real Telegram Desktop, real QA user, local OpenClaw SUT, and a proof plugin mutating `reply_payload_sending`.
- Observed result: Telegram Desktop rendered the bot reply `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK` with the injected portable button labeled `PR 98922 Proof` below the reply.
- TDLib artifact: `tdlib-main-linux-x64.tgz`, SHA-256 `5041fb31995c1da603c8de80a996965c12acdd42bb9970873a622db4db6beea6`.
- Captured local artifacts under `.artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-98922-reply-payload-buttons/live-20260702T203135Z/`:
  - `telegram-user-crabbox-proof.mp4` SHA-256 `81e7535a9ccca0d9e9c345dda8c65249c0e45e0b59faf7badc190dabd35fb897`
  - `telegram-user-crabbox-proof.contact.png` SHA-256 `0fdb548e781fbb7108e988917e8e5f0535eeed650f6d685c6da4fc88ea216dcb`
  - `pr-98922-live-proof-frame-redacted.png` SHA-256 `24a1d951ad72ac2a4d013c77a9286d83029288a1207848545eaa557c2e40b5bb`
- Caveat: the generic proof runner exited `status=fail` because its matcher did not classify this custom plugin-button reply as the expected reply object. The Desktop capture itself shows the behavior this PR needs. Raw logs are intentionally not posted because they contain Telegram identifiers.

Live PR state after the final push:

- CI is green, including `check-prod-types`, `check-lint`, and `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2`
- Merge state is clean/mergeable
- No unresolved GitHub review threads
